answer:
A scanned, image-only PDF blocks go-live because the ingestion pipeline cannot turn the image into searchable text, which in turn fails the citation-reliability gate.

1. **Ingestion failure**: The current ingestion pipeline relies on standard PDF text extraction, which fails on image-only PDFs because there is no embedded text layer, producing empty document models or empty indexes [NL-029-S05][NL-031-S04]. KnowledgeHub expects a text layer before ingestion and cannot index text or generate citation anchors for image-only files [NL-018-S05]. This causes failed ingestion and incomplete text extraction for critical policies [NL-010-S06].

2. **Answer/citation defects**: Without indexed text or citation anchors, TutorChat either returns answers with no citations, or citations point to the entire document/pages instead of a specific section [NL-021-S02]. It may miss content entirely, producing incomplete or unsafe answers [NL-018-S05].

3. **Reliability gate failure**: These incomplete citations fail the go-live validation threshold, which requires 85% citation correctness [NL-031-S04]. This directly violates reliability guidelines [NL-021-S02].

4. **Enterprise go-live blocker**: Compliance/security officers refuse sign-off because users cannot verify answers against exact source sections [NL-021-S02]. For example, BrightPath Healthcare remained restricted to its initial 100-user pilot and could not expand to 6,500 employees until the scanned-PDF issue was resolved [NL-021-S02]. Manual OCR pre-processing by customers is the only current workaround, adding weeks of delay and heavy IT burden [NL-010-S06][NL-018-S05][NL-011-S04]. A permanent automated OCR pipeline was only planned for August 2026 [NL-029-S05][NL-018-S05].
